speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

To proceed accurately, please describe the onset of these symptoms and whether they appeared simultaneously or developed gradually.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete_Blood_Count: WBC 15,000 /μL (elevated), Hemoglobin 14 g/dL, Platelets 300,000 /μL; Erythrocyte_Sedimentation_Rate: NORMAL READINGS; C-Reactive_Protein: NORMAL READINGS.

speaker: Doctor
text: The CBC shows elevated white blood cells indicating an infection, but the normal ESR and CRP are unusual given your fever; can you describe the specific appearance of your skin lesions and exactly where on your wrist the pain is most severe? REQUEST TEST: Antinuclear Antibody (ANA) and Rheumatoid Factor (RF).

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Antinuclear Antibody: NORMAL READINGS; Rheumatoid Factor: NORMAL READINGS.

speaker: Doctor
text: The ANA and Rheumatoid Factor results are normal, which makes an autoimmune cause like Lupus or Rheumatoid Arthritis unlikely despite the fever and wrist pain. Given the high white blood cell count, could you describe if the skin lesions are tender, warm, or if they have any drainage, and do you have a history of recent insect bites or travel? REQUEST TEST: Erythrocyte_Sedimentation_Rate (ESR) with specific inflammatory markers.

speaker: Doctor
text: The repeated normal ESR is puzzling given your fever and elevated white blood cell count; could you describe the specific shape, size, and distribution of the skin lesions and whether you have any joint swelling or morning stiffness? REQUEST TEST: Serum Uric Acid and HLA-B27 genetic test. REQUEST IMAGES: Dermatology_photo_of_skin_lesions.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Serum Uric Acid: NORMAL READINGS; HLA-B27 genetic test: NORMAL READINGS; Dermatology_photo_of_skin_lesions: Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions noted on the dorsum of both wrists and hands; two lesions on the left palm.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The presentation of painless, violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on the wrists, combined with fever and elevated white blood cells but normal inflammatory markers, is highly suggestive of Gianotti-Crosti syndrome or a specific viral exanthem, but the distribution strongly points to a localized dermatologic infection or reaction. Could you describe the nature of the fever and whether you have any lymphadenopathy?

REQUEST IMAGES: Ultrasound of the wrists.
DIAGNOSIS READY: Infectious Erythema (Erythema Infectiosum) or Gianotti-Crosti Syndrome secondary to Parvovirus B19.
